task_specification.objective: Deliver three bounded implementation families that make automatic combat audio, authored cemetery spatial integrity, and dense-run native qualification directly retestable while preserving the native Godot project, host boot, authored map package, and retained combat presentation.

diagnosis.root_cause: Three independent release-convergence failures remain: authoritative lantern attack receipts do not produce a bounded audible Effects-bus report, the authored cemetery perimeter exposes an abrupt void during traversal, and dense-run qualification is blocked by software-renderer evidence despite an existing profile path.

stop_conditions: Do not expand beyond the three required gap families or add deferred backlog work.
Do not replace preserved authored assets or retained source recordings; repair integration, framing, collision, or instrumentation around them.
Host recapture, formal review, issue closure, and phase verdict remain Tester/GameLoop Runtime responsibilities.

strategy.rationale: Partition each required gap and active issue into a distinct root-cause family. Use audio ownership/routing and bounded envelopes instead of transform tuning, authored-map boundary/framing restoration instead of decorative replacement, and deterministic profile readiness with explicit renderer gating instead of claiming unavailable llvmpipe qualification.

code: Run project parse/integrity and boot checks on all modified GDScript and scene resources; verify preserved native_godot_project and host_godot_boot baselines remain runnable.

Run focused static or smoke checks for one-to-one attack audio ownership, upgrade-card value/focus predicates, authored-map anchor/collision alignment, and dense-profile release guards/reset isolation.
runtime: GameLoop Runtime/Tester recaptures automatic combat audio with one SEMI and one quick AUTO input window, inspecting Effects waveform, source-event timeline, runtime logs, and lifecycle reset receipts.

GameLoop Runtime/Tester recaptures authored cemetery spatial traversal from spawn through the critical route and perimeter, pairing screenshots with spatial bounds, collision, landmark visibility, and ordinary movement state.

Host runs the dense prepare/advance/reset protocol under a native renderer at the required viewport and density, then evaluates frame/physics/render/allocation and three-cycle reset evidence; current software-renderer output remains diagnostic only.
visual: Compare shipped gameplay views for coherent cemetery fill, external depth, larger traversable scale, stable central building/landmark, aligned boundary, and no west-edge void or occlusion drift.

Verify the lantern attack remains visually readable through compact bolt/impact VFX without duplicated presentation, and verify upgrade cards show authored silhouettes/icons, concise truthful current-to-new deltas, and distinct keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states.

done_when: One SEMI-equivalent automatic lantern attack and one quick AUTO tap each produce exactly one bounded, recognizable firearm transient in mixed Effects output, with no duplicate full-shot replay.

Native report, adapter report, miss, concrete hit, metal hit, and character-hit stems are distinguishable through candidate receipts or telemetry; a long ringing impact cue cannot mask the firearm report.

AUTO begins only after cadence-valid continuation, stops on release, and resets cleanly on lifecycle reset; compact impact VFX and character-hit feedback remain intact even if unsuitable world-surface impact audio is disabled.

Upgrade choices lead with recognizable authored silhouettes/icons, show truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant deltas, omit unchanged or placeholder NEW/LOCKED current values, and expose complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states.
Tester can directly retest the audio path with one SEMI and one quick AUTO sequence and inspect source-event timing, one-to-one receipts, and the upgrade-card focus/value states.
tasks.instructions: Repair the product-owned lantern combat audio path around the retained component/source audio. Trace the weapon runtime, audio director, and directly related feedback presenter; isolate native report, adapter report, miss, concrete/metal/character hit stems and their Effects routing/envelopes. Remove duplicate replay, clamp or disable unsuitable long world-surface impact cues while preserving compact impact VFX and character-hit feedback, and enforce cadence-valid AUTO lifecycle behavior. In the same presentation boundary, finish the upgrade-card visual hierarchy with authored icon/silhouette leadership, compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new deltas, and keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus styling. Add only candidate-owned receipts needed for black-box plus white-box retest; preserve source recordings and weapon hierarchy.
tasks.title: Restore one-to-one lantern audio and authored choice readability

done_when: The player-visible arena uses the authored cemetery map as the authoritative environment with larger traversable scale and a coherent external world/external depth around the playable perimeter.
The central building/landmark remains visible and stable from spawn, critical route, and cardinal views; no disappearance or camera-occlusion drift occurs during ordinary movement/movement replay.

Player, objective, navigation, and gameplay boundary/collision align to authored streets/terrain; there is no pass-through at the central building or perimeter boundary and no abrupt dark void at the boundary/perimeter.

The authored package remains one intact runtime instance; unrelated proxy/support clutter is removed or minimized, and camera framing stays inside the authored world without hiding or duplicating native geometry.

Tester can replay spawn-to-route movement, inspect spatial bounds/collision, and capture spawn, route, landmark, and perimeter views proving external depth, landmark stability, aligned collision, and boundary integrity.
tasks.instructions: Restore spatial integrity using the already-bound authored cemetery package rather than decorative replacement. Rebase spawn, objective anchors, navigation, collision, and gameplay boundary onto native authored streets/terrain; remove or minimize unrelated proxy/support clutter and frame the external world to eliminate the west-perimeter void. Ensure larger traversable scale, central building/landmark stability, aligned collision, and ordinary movement/movement replay without disappearance or occlusion drift. Keep the complete map as one intact authoritative environment instance and preserve its native materials, props, streets, and landmarks.
tasks.title: Restore authored cemetery scale, boundary, and landmark visibility

done_when: A deterministic dense-run profile can be enabled in an editor/test context and reports frame-time/FPS, physics/render timing, active enemy/projectile/pickup/effect/light/audio counts, allocation or orphan indicators where available, and lifecycle reset markers over the sustained swarm window.
Profile receipts identify renderer identity and explicitly distinguish software-renderer rejection from candidate workload; no qualification pass is claimed from llvmpipe evidence.

The profile is inert in ordinary release runs, has a clear release-build guard, preserves gameplay semantics, and records requested/resolved/reset-isolation, cycle identity, and next-frame reset receipts.

Tester/host can run the same prepare/advance/reset protocol under a native renderer at the required density and compare three-cycle metrics against the dense-run contract without changing boot, combat, HUD, or restart behavior.
tasks.instructions: Harden the candidate-side dense profile only where receipts or guards are incomplete. Keep deterministic prepare/advance/reset entrypoints, bounded sampling, active-work counters, lifecycle reset checks, and renderer classification explicit and low-overhead. Preserve software sessions as rejected evidence while emitting host-usable native qualification receipts; do not tune gameplay or claim native performance from the current llvmpipe environment. Keep all tester-only actions unavailable in release exports.
tasks.title: Prepare deterministic dense-run native qualification evidence
